title: Workers' Compensation Referral Charges, Payers and the Bill Submission Deadline
content:
# Charges, payers and the bill submission deadline

**§1 Fee basis.** Charges on a Workers' Compensation Referral follow the program's fee basis.

**§2 Initial evaluation.** The initial evaluation is billed at the program's evaluation rate where that rate is above $0.00.

**§3 Later dates of service — no longer in force.** The clause under which each later date of service is billed as the program's unit rate times the billing units, with units counted in the program's billing unit and capped at the program's maximum billable units per day (and, for hour-billed programs, between the minimum and maximum daily program hours), is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current basis for billing program days.

**§4 Missed Functional Capacity Evaluation — no longer in force.** The clause under which a missed Functional Capacity Evaluation is billed to the carrier at the program's missed-evaluation fee only where the program bills a missed evaluation to the carrier is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current basis for the missed-evaluation fee.

**§5 Who is billed.** An accepted or without-prejudice claim is billed to the carrier, and a direct-pay program to the employer every employer invoice cycle in calendar days; the worker is never billed for a compensable claim while the program protects the worker from billing on a compensable claim.

**§6 Submission deadline.** A bill is submitted no later than the program's bill submission deadline in calendar days after the date of service; a later bill is written off as an untimely-bill write-off and is never billed to anyone while the program does not allow an untimely bill to be collected.

The figures these clauses read — the unit rate, the evaluation rate and the maximum billable units per day — are the program's own figures, the same for every referral in that program.

## Who is billed (§5 restated)

| Position on the referral record | Billed to |
|---|---|
| Form 60 — accepted | the carrier |
| Form 63 — paid without prejudice | the carrier |
| employer direct program | the employer, on its invoice cycle |

The payer is read from the compensability position on the referral record for this referral.

## Points of judgement

**Is an initial evaluation charged in a program whose evaluation rate is $0.00?** No; §2 bills the evaluation only where the rate is above $0.00.

**A bill goes out one day after the submission deadline has run.** It is written off as an untimely-bill write-off and, in a program where an untimely bill is not collectible, is never billed to anyone — not the carrier, the employer or the worker.

**Can the worker be billed for treatment on an accepted claim?** Not while the program protects the worker from billing on a compensable claim.

A missed Functional Capacity Evaluation is billed to the carrier at fce_no_show_fee only where fce_no_show_billable_to_carrier is true.
